beats.headline: Why are platform threads killing your memory?
beats.subline: OS threads are expensive. Virtual threads are cheap. Let's see why.
beats.narration: Platform threads wrap OS threads, each hogging a megabyte of stack. If you have ten thousand concurrent requests, you're wasting gigabytes of RAM just on thread stacks. Enter Project Loom.

beats.title: Scaling Limits
beats.narration: Platform threads are a one-to-one mapping to the kernel. Virtual threads are managed by the JVM, multiplexing millions of tasks onto a small pool of carrier threads.

beats.title: M:N Scheduling Internals
beats.subtitle: How tasks move between carriers
beats.narration: When a task blocks, the JVM unmounts the virtual thread, saving its stack to the heap. The carrier thread then immediately picks up another ready task. The CPU never sits idle.

beats.title: Spawning Virtual Threads

steps.explanation: Creates one virtual thread per task. No manual pooling needed.
Thread.sleep unmounts the thread, freeing the carrier.

beats.narration: Notice the executor. It spawns a new virtual thread for every single task. Because they are lightweight heap objects, fifty thousand tasks won't crash your JVM.

beats.title: Part 1 Locked In
beats.nextPartTeaser: Up Next (Part 2): The hidden danger of Thread Pinning →
beats.narration: That's the architecture. In Part 2, we tackle Thread Pinning—the silent performance killer that can stall your entire carrier pool.

beats.headline: Why does a synchronized block stall your thread?
beats.subline: Pinning prevents unmounting. Here is how to keep your carriers free.
beats.narration: Virtual threads are supposed to unmount when they block. But if they're pinned, the carrier thread gets stuck too. This is the primary performance trap in Java 21.

beats.title: Pinning vs Clean Unmounting
beats.narration: On Java 21, blocking inside a synchronized block pins the carrier. Use ReentrantLock instead; it's designed to cooperate with the virtual thread scheduler.

beats.title: Detecting Pinning
beats.caption: Spot pinning before it hits production

lines.text: # Run with trace flag to see pinning

beats.narration: Use the tracePinnedThreads flag to dump stack traces when a thread pins. It's the fastest way to find legacy synchronized blocks causing bottlenecks.

beats.title: Java 24+ Evolution

steps.explanation: Object monitors are now virtual-thread aware.

beats.narration: Great news: Java 24 fixed this. The JVM now allows unmounting inside synchronized blocks. If you're on a modern JDK, pinning is mostly a thing of the past.

beats.title: Part 2 Locked In
beats.narration: Pinning is solved. In Part 3, we look at Structured Concurrency—the new way to manage complex parent-child thread lifecycles.

beats.headline: Are your background threads leaking?
beats.subline: Orphan threads are a nightmare. Structured concurrency fixes the lifecycle.
beats.narration: When threads are cheap, you spawn more of them. But if a parent fails, children often keep running, burning resources. Structured concurrency forces a clean hierarchy.

beats.title: StructuredTaskScope
beats.subtitle: Parent-child lifecycle enforcement
beats.narration: The scope ensures that all child threads finish before the parent continues. If one fails, the scope shuts down the others automatically.

beats.title: ShutdownOnFailure Pattern

steps.explanation: Guarantees all children are cleaned up.
Wait for completion or failure signal.

beats.narration: This pattern is bulletproof. If fetchUser fails, the scope cancels fetchInv immediately. No orphan threads, no resource leaks, just clean code.

beats.title: Old vs New Concurrency
beats.narration: ExecutorService is great for background jobs, but for request-response flows, StructuredTaskScope is the new gold standard.

beats.title: Part 3 Locked In
beats.narration: Structured concurrency is the future of Java flow control. In Part 4, we replace the messy ThreadLocal with Scoped Values.

beats.headline: Why ThreadLocal is a memory leak waiting to happen.
beats.subline: Scoped values are immutable, bounded, and perfect for virtual threads.
beats.narration: ThreadLocal is a global variable in disguise. It's mutable, hard to track, and leaks memory when threads are reused. Scoped values fix this for good.

beats.title: ThreadLocal vs ScopedValue
beats.narration: Scoped values are lexically bounded. Once the block ends, the value is gone. No remove calls, no leaks, and it works perfectly with child threads.

beats.title: Using Scoped Values

steps.explanation: Value exists only inside this block.

beats.narration: The value is bound to the current thread and any children it forks. It's immutable, making it thread-safe and incredibly efficient for passing context.

beats.title: Final Recap
beats.caption: Project Loom Summary
beats.narration: Virtual threads, pinning fixes, structured concurrency, and scoped values. You're now equipped to build the next generation of high-concurrency Java apps.
